slot.brief: Four given orders (e.g. ionisation enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, atomic radius, electronegativity) — pick the one that is INCORRECT for the specified set of elements.

stem: Which of the following electronegativity orders is incorrect?

verdicts.working: Electronegativity decreases down a group. The halogen order is F > Cl > Br > I, so option (C) is incorrect.

working:
Electronegativity increases across a period from left to right and decreases down a group. A: F (4.0) > O (3.5) > N (3.0) > C (2.5), correct. B: Cl (3.0) > S (2.5) > P (2.1) > Si (1.8), correct. C: For halogens, the actual order is F (4.0) > Cl (3.0) > Br (2.8) > I (2.5), so I > Br > Cl > F is reversed and incorrect. D: N (3.0) > P (2.1) > As (2.0) > Sb (1.9), correct.

Independent check: Electronegativity decreases down a group. The halogen order is F > Cl > Br > I, so option (C) is incorrect.
solution: Electronegativity decreases down a group. For halogens, the order is $\mathrm{F>Cl>Br>I}$; hence the reverse order $\mathrm{I>Br>Cl>F}$ is incorrect.
